label_policy.closed_world: a row is labelled when it is annotated and has at least one policy term; for such a row a vocabulary term absent from its propagated annotation is a negative; unknown rows and annotated rows with no policy term are not labelled and are never negatives

protocol.adr: ADR-0014 (protocol of ADR-0010, ADR-0011 and ADR-0013)
protocol.early_stopping: negative mean binary cross-entropy on an inner whole-cluster holdout of the training partitions; patience 10, at most 80 epochs
protocol.fmax_rule: precision is averaged over rows with at least one term at or above the threshold, recall over all rows with a vocabulary positive, F = 2PR/(P+R); the threshold is nested (see threshold_rule), so Fmax here is F at the nested threshold, not an oracle maximum
protocol.label_states: annotated or unknown (ADR-0006); never negative; a row is labelled when it is annotated and has at least one policy term; for such a row a vocabulary term absent from its propagated annotation is a negative; unknown rows and annotated rows with no policy term are not labelled and are never negatives
protocol.selection_rule: mean over folds of precision@k (k = metrics.primary_k) over rows with a vocabulary positive; tie-break mean fold Fmax under nested thresholds; then the earlier grid point
protocol.threshold_rule: one global threshold on the propagated score (a term scores at least as high as any descendant); it is the CAFA-style Fmax maximiser over the labelled rows that have a vocabulary positive; fold k is scored with a threshold tuned on the out-of-fold scores of the other validation partitions; the frozen threshold is tuned on all validation rows. The calibrated threshold is tuned the same way on the cross-fitted calibrated scores
